sentences.text: Spinops was a medium-sized ceratopsian dinosaur measuring 4.5 meters in length and weighing 1.3 metric tons. It possessed hooks and spines on the back of its frill, making it evolutionarily close to Centrosaurus and Styracosaurus.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a partial parietal bone that preserves most of the midline bar. The genus name Spinops comes from Latin and Greek words meaning "spine" and "face" due to unique facial ornamentation.
Paleontologist Arthur Smith Woodward initially dismissed the Spinops fossils as "nothing but rubbish".
The fossils were not formally described until 2011, when the species Spinops sternbergorum was named.

Fossils of Spinops were first discovered in 1916 near the Red Deer River in southern Alberta by collectors Charles Hazelius Sternberg and his son Levi Sternberg. These remains are now housed in the Natural History Museum in London.
Spinops is classified within the subfamily Centrosaurinae. The parent group of the genus Spinops is the tribe Centrosaurini.

Spinops lived in North America approximately 76.5 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous. Its fossils date to this same stage and were likely found in the Oldman or Dinosaur Park Formations.
